pr_title: Log defaulted kube-scheduler component config at startup
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR passes the initialized ComponentConfig for kube-scheduler through the framework initialization functions, allowing the default plugin registry (and PluginArgs) to be presented to the user after plugin instantiation is filled out by API defaulting.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #93718

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
kube-scheduler now logs processed component config at startup
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:
```docs

```

issue_context.title: Scheduler should log processed component config
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
When setting a non-default component config (especially custom profiles/plugin configurations), the scheduler should at least log what plugins have been enabled at startup.

**Why is this needed**:
Debugging the scheduler almost always requires knowing what plugins are enabled. Usually, it is safe to assume that the default registry is being used but this is obviously not always the case. Logging the plugin configuration would also match the current behavior which logs custom Policy settings:

```
I0805 14:15:30.692300       1 factory.go:232] Creating scheduler from configuration: {{ } [] [{ImageLocalityPriority 1000 <nil>}] [] 0 false}
```

/sig scheduling
comments:
I would expand it to print the whole configuration.

We print all command line args, so it makes sense.
@alculquicondor good point it should print the whole config
+1 to printing the whole configuration once initialized.

Actually, the hardest part of this task is to print the whole plugins configuration, as the determination of the default plugins happens kind of late in the startup sequence.

Can we make an initial PR that just prints the configuration as produced by API defaulting today?

@alculquicondor I can pick this back up now if you'd like. Any specific timeline or blockers for this?

The only partial blocker is that we don't generate the `.profiles[*].plugins` or `profiles[*].pluginConfig` values until much later after API defaulting.

But having something is better than nothing, which is what we have today :)
PR opened here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96426, sorry for the delay

review_comments: why not just override the completed profiles at this point?
We could, but since it's only necessary if we're logging/writing the config I figured I'd keep that logic in the function
Add a comment to say where this parameter was handled.... but maybe we can do `os.Exit(0)` in `LogOrWriteConfig`?
Add a comment to clarify why is this done.

That's a "what", not a "why" 😉 

I would say something like: "Profiles are processed during Framework instantiation to set default plugins and configurations. Capturing them for logging".
